paper_metadata.title: New ternary equi-atomic refractory medium-entropy alloys with tensile ductility: Hafnium versus titanium into NbTa-based solution

evidence.quote: We demonstrate that based on NbTa as the base solution, ternary equiatomic HfNbTa and TiNbTa single-phase body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solutions are achieved at arc-melted alloy ingots.
A series of alloys with equi-atomic composition of NbTa, TiNbTa, HfNbTa and TiHfNbTa were processed using arc melting.

The arc-melted ingots in weight of about 50 g were fabricated under a Ti-gettered argon atmosphere in a water-cooled copper hearth. They are subjected to several remelting and flipping runs to ensure compositional homogeneity. The effective cooling rate during the solidification of the ingot is on the order of 1 K/s.

evidence.quote: Similarly, the TiHfNbTa MEA also manifests a small fraction of dendritic grains, as shown in Fig. 5 (d). EDX analysis indicates that the chemical composition of the predominant DR are nearly identical to the nominal one, while the ID with minor fraction is enriched in Ti and Hf.

For the NbTa binary solid solution, its σy is 246 ± 14 MPa, comparable to that of pure Nb and Ta [28,29], suggesting that mixing of Nb and Ta does not generate pronounced solution hardening, consistent with previous findings [26,30,31].
The tensile strain to failure, εf, is over 20%, showing the excellent ductility of this alloy.
Alloying the NbTa with Ti to form the TiNbTa MEA nearly doubles the σy to 478 MPa, with only minor reduction of εf.
For ternary HfNbTa, its σy reaches as high as 847 MPa, a three-fold increase over the NbTa binary.
However, the εf is reduced to < 10%.
The TiHfNbTa quaternary produces an intermediate σy of 663 MPa in between the TiNbTa and the HfNbTa, with an εf similar to the latter.

We also show that alloying Hf into the base NbTa solution manifests a much higher strengthening potency compared with Ti. This difference can be rationalized using empirical parameters and models accounting for the size and modulus misfits among constituent elements.
The fracture surface exhibits ductile dimples with different sizes less than 5 μm, typical for microvoids coalescence transverse to the direction of tensile loading.
Thus, the HfNbTa ternary MEA undergoes intergranular fracture during final unstable failure, partially dominated by the cohesive strength of grain boundaries [33].
